Reddit's (NYSE:RDDT) guidance for slower third-quarter 2026 revenue growth looms over its upcoming earnings report, and Reddit stock is taking the biggest selling among social media names. At $136.52, Reddit stock is down 5% in morning trading. The slide signals fading confidence in how long its streak of rapid revenue gains can last.

24/7 Wall St.

Meanwhile, Snap (NYSE:SNAP) stock is down 3% to $6.16, a shallower drop than Reddit's. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stock is up 0.2% to $643.55, holding steady while its two smaller rivals slip. The Global X Social Media ETF (NASDAQ:SOCL) is down 0.8% to $42.44, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.9% to $767.08, so Reddit's slide runs against both its sector fund and the broader market.

When Reddit last reported, management guided third-quarter revenue to $860 million to $870 million, following Q2 2026 sales of $804.9 million that rose 61.1% year over year, according to its SEC filings. It also said it would stop separately reporting logged-in and logged-out daily active users, after weak U.S. logged-in user growth. Advertising is the swing factor this week, after segment revenue of $762 million rose 64% last quarter.

Meta Platforms stock is barely moving, keeping the group's largest company clear of the selling. The Global X Social Media ETF's latest disclosed holdings gave Reddit and Meta Platforms each a large slice of the fund, while Snap carried a smaller weight.

A Reddit user cashed out 745,575 Chase Ultimate Rewards points after his second child was born, ending years of analysis paralysis over finding the perfect redemption.

Flying economy with two kids capped his redemption value at roughly 1.5 cents per point, making cash back more practical than chasing premium travel deals.

He plans to use the cash to max out his 2025 Roth IRA at $7,000, where it could grow tax-free to roughly $53,000 over 30 years.

Read More: Avoid these 13 retirement mistakes before they derail your future (sponsor)

A Reddit user spent years sitting on 745,575 Chase Ultimate Rewards points. That's the rewards currency on credit cards from JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM). He was waiting for the perfect trip. Then his second child was born, and he cashed out the whole balance.

Ground Picture / Shutterstock.com

He titled his r/CreditCards post "Cashed out 745,575 Chase UR points... and I feel oddly free." I think he made the right call for his situation. What decided it was how his family actually travels.

Years of Analysis Paralysis

He said he'd held the points "forever with nonstop analysis paralysis." He also admitted that "the whole 'wait for the perfect redemption' mindset had me in denial that I'd ever actually use them."

Points don't earn interest, and they don't compound. Until you redeem them, all they do is sit there. A balance you keep planning to use but never do adds nothing to your finances.

Two Kids, Economy Seats and a 1.5-Cent Reality

Several things changed when his second child arrived. His first was 2 years old, which meant the family was losing its lap baby option. A lap baby is a young child who flies on a parent's lap rather than in a paid seat. From then on, every trip would mean buying more seats.

title: 3 Reasons to Buy Reddit Stock This Week
detail:
3 Reasons to Buy Reddit Stock This Week
Rick Munarriz, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 8:23 AM EDT 5 min read
RDDT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

It's showtime for Reddit (NYSE: RDDT) and its investors. Shares of the company behind the popular online forum with more than half a billion users reports its third-quarter results after Thursday's market close.

Expectations are high. The stock price is low. There are some pretty good reasons to be hopeful for a big bounce on Friday, but hold your optimism in check. There are still some serious red flags waving in the wind. Still, I think it's good to warm up to the "community of communities" platform operator. Let's break down the reasons it could be a good buy this week ahead of its telltale financials.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Reddit is historically cheap

Reddit stock has gone cold after a pair of monster rallies since going public in early 2024. The shares are trading 37% lower in 2027, down nearly half from their peak 13 months ago.

A stock doesn't slide in a vacuum. There are some potential potholes to watch for -- and I will get there, eventually -- but few things excite me as much as a stock that's sliding despite strong fundamentals. Reddit's business is booming.

Revenue soared 61% in Reddit's latest quarter, its eighth consecutive quarter of better than 60% top-line growth. Earnings, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), and free cash flow more than doubled. You would think that the price of admission for this high-octane performance would be a healthy market premium. Spoiler alert: Reddit is cheaper than you think.

RDDT data: YCharts.

Reddit is now trading for almost 20 times next year's earnings, but less than 15 times the bottom-line target for 2028. This is near a historical low for Reddit, admittedly, given its short time as a public company. Growth should slow from here, but shouldn't a company posting this kind of growth be worth a healthy premium to the market?

2. Reddit is an earnings season beast

Reddit has now gone through 10 earnings seasons as a publicly traded company. It has consistently topped Wall Street revenue and profit targets. But that doesn't mean stretching that winning streak to 11 will send the shares higher.

Reddit stock has fallen the day after reporting quarterly results in roughly half of its updates. Sometimes there are valuation concerns. With that off the table now, the deal-breaker has been a lack of long-term visibility.

title: Is Reddit (RDDT) Below Fair Value As Earnings Near And Ad Growth Faces Questions?
detail:
Is Reddit (RDDT) Below Fair Value As Earnings Near And Ad Growth Faces Questions?
Simply Wall St
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 10:16 PM EDT 6 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit (RDDT) heads into its 29 October 2026 earnings release with investors focused on the extent to which its recent advertising strength can be sustained as user growth in the United States remains relatively modest.

Reddit's share price has retreated over the year, with the stock down 10.95% on a 90 day share price basis and 37.88% year to date, while the 1 year total shareholder return is down 25.18%. This suggests recent advertising headlines have not yet shifted investor caution around execution and risk.

Scan how Reddit's ad story compares with other platforms chasing monetisation over user growth by reviewing the curated list of 20 high quality undiscovered gems.

Reddit's slide sets up a simple tension. Are investors repricing a business that has run ahead of its fundamentals, or is sentiment resetting while the underlying earnings story moves on a different track?

Most Popular Narrative: 51.5% Undervalued

Against Reddit's last close at $150.26, the most followed narrative pegs fair value around $309.77 per share. That creates a sizable gap between where the market is pricing the stock and what that narrative expects from the earnings and user base.

Successful ad networks are driven fundamentally by usage. The best type of usage is returning daily users, usually measured by Daily Active Users. The higher the number of unique daily active users, the higher the ad revenue generated on a per-day basis. While ad networks, profitability and growth are generally optimised through delivery, for example FB size, scale and optimisations, in the early stage of a company sheer user number and therefore impressions drive a huge part of the narrative for ad spenders to use the platform. RDDT currently represents a large undervalued segment because its DAU user growth is still being undervalued. In the most recent quarterly reports, the company reported total Daily Active Uniques (DAUq) of 126.8 million for Q1 2026, representing a 17% year-over-year increase, highlighting continued strength in user engagement and platform relevance. Importantly, that engagement is increasingly being monetized. Reddit delivered revenue of $663 million in the quarter, up 69% year-over-year and ahead of analyst expectations, signaling strong demand across its advertising and data licensing initiatives.

See why 28 investors see Reddit as 51% undervalued.

According to kinnth, this valuation view leans heavily on the idea that Reddit's daily usage, ad inventory and data licensing can support a higher long term earnings profile than the current share price implies. That narrative applies a discount rate of 8.68% to those projected cash flows and arrives at a fair value that suggests the stock is 51.5% below where it could trade if that thesis plays out.
